title: The Most Important Factory in America by Dan Wang in NYT 23 Oct 2026
gist: A forum post excerpting Dan Wang's NYT essay argues TSMC Arizona matters chiefly because it transfers process knowledge the U.S. has lost, not capital or equipment. TSMC, valued at $2 trillion, plans more than a quarter of a trillion dollars for 10 fabs, two packaging plants and an R&D site in Arizona, employs over 3,500 there, and is exploring Texas, while Taiwan concentration keeps a war discount on the stock.

insights.claim: TSMC, the world's most advanced chipmaker and supplier to Apple and Nvidia, has a $2 trillion market cap that might be higher if it did not make nearly all its chips in Taiwan, which China's Communist Party covets.
insights.speaker: Dan Wang
insights.so_what: Geopolitical risk is an explicit valuation discount on TSMC that U.S. capacity could narrow.
insights.quote: It might be worth even more if TSMC didn’t manufacture nearly all of its chips in Taiwan

insights.claim: When investment banks model a war over Taiwan, they use phrases like global economic depression, trillions in losses and sometimes World War III.
insights.speaker: Dan Wang
insights.so_what: A Taiwan conflict is a systemic tail risk for markets, not just for semis.

insights.claim: TSMC announced its Arizona fab in 2020, drawn by proximity to U.S. customers, federal subsidies and political pressure from the Trump administration, which touts it as the largest foreign direct investment ever into the United States.
insights.speaker: Dan Wang
insights.so_what: Subsidies and political pressure are effective levers for reshoring chip capacity.

insights.claim: In July, TSMC announced plans to invest more than a quarter of a trillion dollars in Arizona for 10 chip plants, two packaging facilities and an R&D site; it employs over 3,500 people there and its CEO said this month it is exploring a Texas investment.
insights.speaker: Dan Wang
insights.so_what: Massive multi-year capex supports U.S. fab equipment, construction and packaging suppliers.

themes.theme: Process knowledge as America's missing asset

insights.claim: The U.S. invented the semiconductor and dominated the industry for decades, but chipmakers like Intel and Texas Instruments fell behind and AI hardware is now made mostly in East Asia.
insights.speaker: Dan Wang
insights.so_what: U.S. legacy chipmakers lost manufacturing leadership, explaining dependence on foreign foundries.
insights.locator: The United States invented the semiconductor

insights.claim: TSMC Arizona's most important contribution is process knowledge, not money, equipment or jobs, because the U.S. lacks the practiced skill of manufacturing rather than capital or access to advanced tools.
insights.speaker: Dan Wang
insights.so_what: Reshoring success depends on skills transfer, so watch workforce and yield parity at U.S. fabs.
insights.quote: What America really lacks is skill
insights.locator: TSMC Arizona is rebuilding America’s manufacturing
